name: Machine-learning service: training, registry, serving, monitoring
summary: Models are trained from versioned data, tracked and registered in MLflow, served behind a typed HTTP API, and watched for drift. Features come from one definition for training and serving.

fitsWhen.says: the data is historical or time-series

avoidWhen.says: a hosted language model would do the job

ai-ml.why: Deep models in PyTorch; scikit-learn or XGBoost are often better on tabular data.

data.why: Training data, features and retraining as scheduled assets.

backend.why: A typed prediction API that loads the model version the registry marks as production.

observability.why: Data and prediction drift reports on the prediction log.

infra.why: Serving as containers; training jobs on a GPU machine or Ray.

ci-cd.why: Tests, a training smoke run and image builds.

testing.why: Unit tests plus a fixed evaluation set that must not regress.

hosting.why: GPUs for training where needed; CPU for serving small models.

services.name: training
responsibilities: Logs runs and registers models in MLflow

services.name: registry
responsibilities: Experiment tracking and the model registry

services.name: monitoring
responsibilities: Compares recent predictions to the training data

dataStores.name: meta-db
dataStores.purpose: MLflow backend and the prediction log

environments.name: dev
environments.purpose: Notebooks and small runs on a laptop

environments.name: staging
environments.purpose: Shadow serving: the candidate model sees real traffic, its answers are logged only

stages.name: smoke-train
stages.does: Train on a tiny sample to catch pipeline breaks

stages.name: evaluate
stages.does: Candidate must beat the current model on the fixed set

notes: Latency and error rate of the prediction API

security.auth: Service-to-service tokens; the prediction API is not public
notes: Personal data minimised in features and prediction logs

folderLayout:
training/
  datasets.py
  train.py
  evaluate.py
serving/

features/
  feature_repo/
monitoring/
notebooks/
conventions: Every model version traces back to a dataset version and a commit
Serving code never trains; training code never serves
A promotion needs an evaluation report

adrs.title: A registry decides what is in production
adrs.decision: Serving loads the model MLflow marks as Production.
adrs.why: Rollback is a registry change, not a redeploy.

adrs.title: One feature definition
adrs.decision: Features are defined once in Feast.
adrs.why: Training-serving skew is the most common silent failure.

repos.label: ml
repos.layout: Training, serving, features and monitoring in one repository
